extracted.intended_audience: offshore renewable energy lessees, grant holders, developers, and their legal/compliance teams
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards for site assessment, construction, operation, and decommissioning of offshore renewable energy facilities on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS), including SAP/COP/GAP submissions, CVA processes, and survey requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site assessment term and SAP timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A commercial lease has a term of five years for the lessee to conduct site assessment activities and to submit a COP; the five-year site assessment term begins upon approval of the SAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAP approval does not authorize building or installing facilities for commercial energy production. COP must be submitted at least 6 months before the five-year site assessment term expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site Assessment Plan (SAP) contents and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Before installing any facilities for site assessment activities on its commercial lease, a lessee must submit a SAP for BOEM approval; the SAP 'describes the activities (e.g., installation of [met] towers, [met] buoys) [the lessee] plan[s] to perform for the characterization of [its] commercial lease...'. The SAP must include the information required by 30 CFR 585.610–585.611.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may request additional information during review and specify terms and conditions that must be incorporated into the SAP before approval. SAP facilities are subject to decommissioning under subpart I and require financial assurance. All site assessment activities must be performed under a safety management system (SMS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and Operations Plan (COP) submission and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Before fabricating and installing any facility for commercial operations, a lessee must submit a COP for BOEM review and approval. The COP must describe the facilities the lessee will construct or use for commercial operations (including project easements and associated onshore/support facilities) and all proposed activities (construction, commercial operations, decommissioning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The COP must include general structural and project design, fabrication, and installation information for each structure, as well as results of geological, geotechnical, biological, and archaeological surveys. BOEM may approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Activities Plan (GAP) requirements for limited leases/ROW/RUE
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities conducted under a limited lease, ROW, or RUE must be approved by BOEM under a GAP, submitted no later than 12 months after the date of lease or grant issuance. The GAP must describe facilities to be constructed or used, project easements, onshore/support facilities, and the design, fabrication, construction, use, and decommissioning of those facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP must include geological, geotechnical, biological, and archaeological survey results. BOEM may approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications and will determine whether proposed facilities are complex or significant; if complex, subpart G applies before activities begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM determination of 'complex or significant' facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will determine if the proposed facilities described in the SAP, COP, or GAP are complex or significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If BOEM determines facilities are not complex/significant, the lessee may begin proposed site assessment activities when BOEM approves the SAP/GAP. If BOEM determines they are complex/significant, the lessee must comply with additional requirements in subpart G of 30 CFR part 585 before beginning activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Management System (SMS) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of activities described in the SAP, whether or not deemed complex or significant, is required to follow a safety management system (SMS) that accounts for and mitigates risks to personnel and the environment associated with such activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved activities under subpart H must be conducted to ensure safety, prevent undue harm to natural resources, use trained personnel, and comply with approved plans. Subpart H contains operational requirements including SMS, incident reporting, inspections, and self-inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart G: design, fabrication, and installation information for complex/significant facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart G requires detailed design, fabrication, and installation information for each complex or significant facility that a lessee or grant holder proposes to operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure facilities operate in a safe manner using accepted engineering practices in conformance with approved plans. Subpart G achieves this primarily by requiring independent assessment by certified verification agents (CVAs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified Verification Agent (CVA) qualifications and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The CVA should be 'experienced in the design, fabrication, and installation of offshore marine facilities or structures' and will conduct specified third-party reviews, inspections, and verifications. Although hired by the lessee or grant holder, the CVA reports directly to BOEM and must not act in a capacity that creates a conflict of interest or the appearance of a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart G outlines circumstances necessitating a CVA, nomination and waiver processes, and CVA duties. BOEM will approve or disapprove CVA nomination or waiver during SAP/COP/GAP review. If waived, the project engineer must perform the same duties and responsibilities as the CVA, except without independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Design Report (FDR) certification
rubrics_metrics.description: After obtaining BOEM approval of the SAP, COP, or GAP, a lessee or grant holder must submit an FDR describing the final design of all proposed facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CVA must certify that the facilities are designed to withstand the environmental and functional load conditions appropriate for the intended service life at the proposed location and must use good engineering judgment in assessing commissioning of critical safety systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabrication and Installation Report (FIR) and CVA certification of fabrication/installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any fabrication (e.g., assembly) or installation of facility components on the OCS, a lessee or grant holder must submit an FIR describing how the facilities will be fabricated and installed consistent with accepted industry standards, the approved SAP/COP/GAP, and the FDR. The FIR must also describe how fabrication of components that took place outside of the OCS is consistent with standards and approved plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CVA must certify that the facilities were fabricated and installed properly. Fabrication of facility components outside the OCS does not require submittal of an FDR and FIR, but the CVA still must certify fabrication/installation. Activities may begin 30 calendar days after BOEM deems submitted the CVA's fabrication and installation certification unless BOEM objects; any objections must be resolved to BOEM's satisfaction before commencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of activities following CVA certification and BOEM objection process
rubrics_metrics.description: The lessee or grant holder may begin approved activities 30-calendar days after BOEM deems submitted the fabrication and installation certification from the CVA, unless BOEM objects in the interim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If BOEM objects to the CVA verification report, the lessee or grant holder must resolve those objections to BOEM's satisfaction before commencing approved activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decommissioning obligations and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when otherwise authorized by BOEM, lessees and grant holders must decommission (i.e., remove) all facilities and clear the seafloor of all obstructions created by their activities within 2 years following termination of their lease or grant or earlier if BOEM determines a facility is no longer useful for operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart I sets forth BOEM's decommissioning requirements and process; BOEM may require financial assurance to cover decommissioning costs. Proposed changes may align decommissioning of met buoys with USACE requirements in lieu of BOEM decommissioning plans in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey requirements (geological, geotechnical, biological, archaeological) for SAP/GAP/COP
rubrics_metrics.description: The SAP, GAP, and COP must include results of geological, geotechnical, biological, and archaeological surveys undertaken in support of the project or proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM requires COPs to include geotechnical survey data used to investigate sediments affecting foundations/anchoring systems, including in situ testing, boring, and sampling at each foundation location and at least one deep boring at each edge of the project area. Lessees must apply for a regulatory departure under § 585.103 if they wish to defer certain geotechnical testing until the FDR stage. Archaeological survey results must be submitted with the COP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological buoy (met buoy) regulatory treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would eliminate BOEM's SAP requirement for site assessment facilities that do not use an engineered foundation (primarily met buoys); met buoys would be exempt from the SAP requirement unless deployed with an engineered foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee still must operate met buoys under an SMS. BOEM would recommend consultation with BOEM and other Federal agencies for novel anchoring technologies absent a BOEM-approved SAP. BOEM proposes aligning decommissioning of met buoys with USACE NWP 5 procedures and generally would not routinely require supplemental financial assurance for met buoy decommissioning when USACE authorizes and enforces removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of duplicative regulation and reliance on USACE NWP 5
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM recognizes that met buoy deployment is subject to USACE permitting under NWP 5 and that BOEM's SAP/GAP requirements can be duplicative for met buoys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule would remove BOEM's SAP requirement for met buoys so deployment would proceed under USACE NWP 5 (or district equivalent), which addresses environmental, archaeological, safety, and navigation impacts and removal/restoration requirements. BOEM will still prepare NEPA analysis and consult under ESA prior to lease sale, and lessees must ensure placement conforms with NWP 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Clean Air Act (CAA) permitting implications for met buoys
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CAA, an 'OCS source' on the OCS that meets certain criteria must apply for an air permit. Met buoys with backup diesel generators have at times been included as OCS sources requiring a CAA permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule anticipates that met buoys deployed under USACE authority and outside BOEM authorization could fall outside the CAA definition of an 'OCS source', potentially removing the need for an OCS air permit in certain USEPA-jurisdiction areas. BOEM did not include potential CAA permit savings in its economic analysis because that burden arises from another agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-lease site assessment authorization and limited lease requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would clarify that off-lease site assessment facilities do not require a limited lease by amending § 585.104 to state that, for purposes of that section, site assessment activities neither produce, transport, nor support the generation of any energy products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM would cease case-by-case determinations about whether off-lease site assessment activities require a lease. USACE permitting would continue to apply for off-lease activities; BOEM believes this change will decrease time/cost to deploy off-lease site assessment facilities and encourage more data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Design Envelope (PDE) use in COPs
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would codify the use of project design envelopes (PDE)—proposing a range of design parameters and construction and operation activities—in COP submissions, allowing lessees to submit a reasonable range of design parameters within their permit application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM will analyze the maximum impacts from the PDE range for NEPA. A PDE should not be overly broad so the project is sufficiently defined for meaningful analysis. BOEM may approve the full PDE or restrict certain scenarios if environmental impacts are unacceptable. The PDE can include non-design attributes (e.g., installation methods, mitigation measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM review process flexibility and requests for additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may request additional information during review of SAPs, GAPs, and COPs and may specify terms and conditions that must be incorporated before approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM's review contemplates approval, disapproval, or approval with modifications. BOEM may attach stipulations to future leases relating to site assessment activities not covered by a SAP to ensure awareness and conformance with USACE requirements and best industry practices.
